name: Durham University
summary: A collegiate university in a small historic city in north-east England; about 170 undergraduate courses, and each student joins a college.

ib.text: Offers are a total including three HL grades, from 31 (555) to 38 (776); an AAA course asks 36 with 666 at HL. Some courses name HL subjects and grades.

TMUA (strongly encouraged, Maths): booking for January sitting closes, 18:00 UK time
LNAT (Law): register, book and sit the test for Durham
UCAS equal consideration deadline, 18:00 UK time

programmes.name: Natural Sciences
programmes.about: A flexible science degree for interests that span several subjects, including at least one science. You combine Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Maths, Computer Science and more, with optional Anthropology, Business, Geography or Philosophy. A year abroad or placement can extend it to four years.
programmes.ib: 37 points with 766 at HL, one of them in a science. Named HL grades apply: Maths 7 for Mathematics; 6 or 7 in Maths and Physics for Physics; 6 in Maths for Computer Science.

needs.note: One HL science; some subject choices name grades and subjects

programmes.selectionNote: Offers depend on the subjects you combine; your whole UCAS application is read. Most Durham courses use no admissions test. You also join a college.

flagshipSource.title: Natural Sciences BSc: combine at least one science with subjects from three groups, with year abroad or placement

programmes.name: Archaeology
programmes.about: World archaeology from earliest prehistory to the modern day, with training in social and scientific methods. Excavation, fieldwork, osteology, 3D modelling and museum and heritage skills are covered, and you can follow a route accredited by the Chartered Institute for Archaeologists.
programmes.ib: 35 points with 665 at HL. No HL subject is required.
programmes.selectionNote: No admissions test is listed. Your whole UCAS application, including the personal statement, is read. You also join a college.

flagshipSource.title: Archaeology BA: world archaeology with fieldwork, lab skills and a CIfA-accredited route

programmes.name: Law
programmes.about: A research-led LLB in the law of England and Wales that forms the first stage of training as a solicitor or barrister. Optional modules let you specialise in public or private law, including international law, and there is a moot court and a pro bono room.
programmes.ib: 37 points with 766 at HL. No HL subject is required.
programmes.selectionNote: The LNAT is essential: register, book and sit it in the year you apply, linking Durham to your LNAT account. The multiple-choice score and essay are read with your UCAS form.

flagshipSource.title: Law LLB: research-led teaching with a moot court, a pro bono room and a choice of specialist pathways

faculties.name: Faculty of Arts and Humanities
faculties.line: English, History, Classics, Music, Philosophy, Theology and languages, alone or combined; an AAA degree asks 36 points with 666 at HL.

faculties.name: Faculty of Science
faculties.line: Natural Sciences asks 37 with 766 at HL, one in a science, with named grades by subject; Mathematics asks HL Maths 7.

faculties.name: Faculty of Social Sciences and Health
faculties.line: Entry varies by department: Law asks 37 with 766 and the LNAT; Archaeology 35 with 665 and no set subject.

faculties.name: Durham University Business School
faculties.line: Economics: 37 points with 766 at HL, including Maths; SL Maths at 7 is accepted if you do not take it at HL.

notes: Every student is a member of a college, and Durham guarantees an offer of accommodation to first-years who apply for it.
Most courses need no admissions test, but Law and Mathematics applicants are strongly encouraged to sit the LNAT or a maths test (TMUA or STEP).
